question:
Direction: Choose the option that is in the direct form of the sentence.

He told her that he preferred tea to coffee.
options: He said to her, "He preferred tea to coffee."
He asked her, "Do you prefer tea to coffee?"
He told her, "You prefer tea to coffee."
He said to her, "I prefer tea to coffee."
Question Not Attempted
solution:
The direct form of the given sentence is 'He said to her, "I prefer tea to coffee."

Key Points

  • While changing a sentence from indirect speech to direct speech, we need to follow these steps-
    • The conjunction 'that' will be replaced with a comma (,) and inverted commas (" ").
    • 'Told' remains either unchanged or changed into 'said to'.
    • The past indefinite tense (v2- preferred) is changed into the present indefinite tense (v1- prefer).
    • The third-person (he) is changed into 'I' i.e. according to the subject of the reporting verb (He).
       
The final sentence- He said to her, "I prefer tea to coffee."

question:

options: He said to me, "Gandhi Ji starts the Salt Movement."
He said to me, "Gandhi Ji started the Salt Movement."
He said to me, "Gandhi Ji had started the Salt Movement."
He said to me, "Gandhi Ji has started the Salt Movement."
Question Not Attempted
solution:
The direct form of the given sentence is 'He said to me, "Gandhi Ji started the Salt Movement."

Key Points

  • While changing a sentence from indirect speech to direct speech, we need to follow these steps-
    • The conjunction 'that' will be replaced with a comma (,) and inverted commas (" ").
    • 'Told' remains either unchanged or changed to 'said to'.
    • If the reported speech is a universal fact, historical event, scientific fact, habitual action, etc., the tense of the reported speech does not change.
    • The given sentence is a historical event, hence, its tense will not be changed.
       
The final sentence- He said to me, "Gandhi Ji started the Salt Movement."

question:
Direction: Choose the option that is in the direct form of the sentence.

The doctor advised him to do exercises daily for at least thirty minutes.
options: The doctor said to him, "Do exercises daily for at least thirty minutes."
The doctor said to him, "You should exercises daily for at least thirty minutes."
The doctor said to him, "To do exercises daily for at least thirty minutes."
The doctor said to him, "You did exercises daily for at least thirty minutes."
Question Not Attempted
solution:
The direct form of the given sentence is 'The doctor said to him, "Do exercises daily for at least thirty minutes."

Key Points

  • The sentence which is used to convey a command, a request, or a forbiddance is called an imperative sentence. So the given speech is an imperative one
  • While changing an imperative sentence from indirect speech to direct speech, we need to follow these steps-
    • The conjunction 'to' will be replaced with a comma (,) and inverted commas (" ").
    • 'Advised' is changed into 'said to'.
    • At last line up the remaining part.
       
The final sentence- The doctor said to him, "Do exercises daily for at least thirty minutes."

question:

solution:

Key Points

  • The sentence which is used to convey a command, a request, or a forbiddance is called an imperative sentence. So the given speech is an imperative one
  • While changing an imperative sentence from indirect speech to direct speech, we need to follow these steps-

question:
Out of the given options, choose the one which is the correct direct speech of the sentence given below.

My teacher often says to me that if I don't work hard I shall fail.
options: My teacher often says to me, “If you didn't work hard, you shall fail.”
My teacher often says to me, “If you don't work hard, you will fail.”
My teacher often says to me, “If you doesn't work hard, you will fail.”
My teacher often said to me, “If you don't work hard, you will fail.”
Question Not Attempted
solution:
The direct speech is My teacher often says to me, “If you don't work hard, you will fail.”

Additional Information

  • Let's look at the steps to change the sentence from direct to indirect speech:
  • When the indirect speech is in an assertive form, we follow the steps given below:
    • The reporting verb 'says to' will remain the same as per the given options.
    • Connector 'that' is replaced by a comma and inverted commas.
    • The tense of indirect/reported speech will remain the same as the reporting verb(says) is in the present tense.
    • The auxiliary verb don't will remain the same as per the pronoun 'you' whereas 'shall' gets converted into 'will' according to the pronoun 'you'.
    • The personal pronouns will be changed according to the subject and object of the reporting verb.
    • ​Here the 1st person 'I' will change into the 2nd person 'you' as per the object.
  • ​At last line up the remaining part.
     

Following these steps, we finally get- My teacher often says to me, “If you don't work hard, you will fail.”

Additional Information  ​​​​

  • In the case of a general truth or universal fact, there will be no change in the tense of reported speech.

question:
Choose the correct indirect narration of the following sentence:

'Do you wish to open an account?' the accountant said to the man.
options: The accountant asked the man that he wished to open an account
The accountant asked the man if he wished to open an account
The accountant questioned the man that he wished to open an account
The accountant asked the man if you wished to open an account
Question Not Attempted
solution:
The correct answer is 'The accountant asked the man if he wished to open an account.'

 Key Points

  • Indirect speech is used to report what someone has said, without quoting their exact words.
  • In indirect questions, we often use "if" or "whether" to introduce the question.
  • The verb "asked" is appropriate for reporting a question.
  • The subject "he" refers to "the man" in the original sentence.
  • Hence the sentence becomes 'The accountant asked the man if he wished to open an account.'

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

question:
Select the correct indirect form of the given sentence.

She said, “She must leave all the bad habits.”
options: She said she has to leave all the bad habits
She said that she must have leave all the bad habits
She said that she had to leave all the bad habits.
She said that she could leave all the bad habits
Question Not Attempted
solution:
The correct answer is: She said that she had to leave all the bad habits.

Key Points 

  • The given sentence is in direct speech and we need to convert it to indirect speech.
  • When we change a direct speech to an indirect speech, we must follow these rules:
    • The reporting verb "said" remains unchanged in the indirect speech.
    • The inverted commas ("...") are replaced with the conjunction 'that' to show the indirect speech part.
    • The comma (,) is removed in the indirect speech.
    • The first word of the indirect speech should be in capital letters.
    • 'Must' in direct speech changes to 'Had to' in indirect speech.
  • Thus, option 3 is the correct answer.
     

Hence, indirect speech is - She said that she had to leave all the bad habits.

 

Important Points

  • 'MUST changes into HAD TO' from direct speech to indirect speech
    • He said, “I must study for the exam”. - He said that he had to study the exam.
    • She said, “I must finish the work in time”.- She said that she had to finish the work in time.

question:
Select the correct indirect form of the given sentence.

"Sara said to John, 'I am practicing for the concert.'"
options: Sara told John that she was practicing for the concert.
Sara told John that she is practicing for the concert.
Sara told John that she had been practicing for the concert.
Sara told John that she practices for the concert.
Question Not Attempted
solution:
The correct answer is 'Sara told John that she was practicing for the concert.'

Key Points

  • The conjunction "that" is used in the indirect speech to join the main part of the sentence and the reported part, which replaces the comma from the direct speech.
  • The verb "said to" is changed to "told" in indirect speech.
  • The first person pronoun "I" in direct speech is changed to the third person pronoun "she" in the indirect speech to match the subject.
  • Here, "am practicing" in present continuous tense becomes "was practicing" in past continuous tense in the indirect speech.

Therefore, the correct answer is 'option 1'.

question:

solution:
The correct answer is 'David told James that he could not come to the party that night.'

Key Points

  • In the indirect speech, the conjunction 'that' is used to connect the reporting verb with the reported speech.
  • When the speech is converted to indirect, the inverted commas are removed.
  • The pronoun 'I' is changed to 'he' in the indirect form.
  • The modal verb 'can' is changed to 'could' in the indirect speech because indirect speech usually requires backshift of tenses.

  • The time indication 'tonight' is changed to 'that night' in indirect speech. 

Therefore, the correct answer is 'option 1'.

question:
Convert the sentence in Indirect speech:
Tom Cruise said, "My God, what madness has taken over you!"
options: Tom Cruise exclaimed with disbelief that madness had taken over him.
Tom Cruise yelled with fear about what madness has taken over him.
Tom Cruise exclaimed with disbelief that such madness had taken over him.
Tom Cruise questioned with disbelief that what is the madness that has taken over him.
Question Not Attempted
solution:
The correct answer is 'Tom Cruise exclaimed with disbelief that madness had taken over him.'

Key Points

  • Converting direct speech into indirect speech involves changing the grammar and structure of the sentence to reflect a report of the original statement, rather than directly quoting that statement.
  • The original sentence from Tom Cruise includes an exclamation of disbelief and concern over someone else's behavior, which is encapsulated by the phrase, "My God, what madness has taken over you!"
  • In indirect speech, expressions of surprise or strong emotion, such as "My God," typically lead to the use of verbs like "exclaimed" to convey the intensity of the speaker's feelings.
  • The direct question "what madness has taken over you" is transformed into a statement in indirect speech, and it shifts from addressing "you" to talking about "him," consistent with the change in perspective from direct dialogue to reported speech.
  • The statement accurately captures the essence and urgency of the original exclamation without directly posing it as a question, which aligns with the conventions of converting from direct to indirect speech.
  • Use of the term "madness" in both sentences keeps the focus on the inexplicable or unreasonable behavior that prompted Tom Cruise's exclamation.
  • The introduction doesn't need to specify the type or reason for the madness, as the emphasis is on the disbelief and shock at the behavior itself, which is accurately reflected in the converted statement.

Therefore, the correct answer is "option 1".

question:
The doctor said, "Do you have a headache now?"

The sentence can be written in indirect speech as:-
options: The doctor asked the patient if he had a headache then.
The doctor asked the patient if he has a headache now.
The doctor asked the patient if he had a headache now.
The doctor asked the patient that he had a headache then.
Question Not Attempted
solution:
The correct answer is 'The doctor asked the patient if he had a headache then.'
 
Key Points
  • Rule: In Indirect Speech, the tense of the verb in the reported speech is changed to match past tense of the reporting verb. Here, 'do have' becomes 'had'.
  • Rule: A question in direct speech becomes a statement in indirect speech. The interrogative form of the sentence changes to the assertive form. Hence, 'Do you have' changes appropriately to 'if he had'.
  • Rule: The words expressing nearness in time or place in Direct Speech are generally changed into words expressing distance in Indirect Speech. Therefore, 'now' changes to 'then'.
  • The structure of the Indirect Speech in this context is: reporting verb + object + conjunction (if or whether) + subject + verb.
    • Example: "The doctor asked the patient if he had a headache then".
Therefore, the correct answer is 'Option 1'.
 
Additional Information
  • 'The doctor asked the patient if he has a headache now.' is incorrect because the verb tense hasn't been appropriately changed from present ('has') to past ('had') according to the conversion rule.
  • 'The doctor asked the patient if he had a headache now.' is incorrect because the time reference 'now' should be converted to 'then' in indirect speech.
  • 'The doctor asked the patient that he had a headache then.' is incorrect because it's not properly structured as a question in the indirect speech. The word 'that' doesn't suit this context; 'if' would be more appropriate.
